tests.definition: Two rooms of 10 m by 10 m are joined by a corridor 10 m long and 2 m wide, which starts and ends at the centre of one side of each room. One hundred occupants with no pre-evacuation time and speeds drawn from the building population start in room 1, packed from the left at the highest possible density, and move to room 2. The time the last of them enters room 2 is recorded. The run is repeated with 10, 50 and 100 additional occupants of the same kind starting in room 2 and moving to room 1 at the same time. The tester discusses how large the time increases are and documents any long-term blocking.
tests.expected: The recorded time increases with the number of occupants in counter-flow. ISO calls the evaluation qualitative and sets no numeric limit.
deviations: Decision D10: a level in which some room-1 occupant does not reach room 2 within the 200 s budget is reported as 'blocking documented'. It counts as later than every level that completes, as ISO asks for blocking to be documented and not treated as a failure.

The pass rule is the suite's own: the last room-2 entry times of the levels that complete must increase strictly, no completing level may follow a blocked one, and the level without counter-flow must complete. Room 2 is entered at the first frame with x of 20 m or more, the far end of the corridor.
All occupants walk at a constant 1.2 m/s instead of a speed distribution from the building population.

The 100 room-1 occupants start at random positions in a 2.5 m by 9.6 m strip along the left wall (mean density about 4.2 persons per square metre), which may be below the maximum possible density. Counter-flow occupants start in a strip against the right wall. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Overtaking people with movement disabilities
tests.definition: Room 1 (5 m by 4 m) and room 2 (5 m by 4 m) are joined by a ramp 12 m long and 1.5 m wide, with a 1 m exit at the end of room 2. Room 1 contains zone 1, which holds 24 occupants walking at 1.25 m/s with the model's default body size, and zone 2, a 1 m strip at the ramp entrance. In Scenario 1 zone 2 holds one occupant with a disability: 0.8 m/s on flat ground, 0.4 m/s on the ramp, occupying more than half the ramp width (0.75 m), for example a wheelchair user. In Scenario 2 the zone-2 occupant is like the other 24. Everyone must reach the exit. A model that cannot represent such occupants documents that limitation.
tests.expected: The zone-1 occupants reach the exit later in Scenario 1 than in Scenario 2. ISO calls the test a qualitative verification of emergent behaviour and sets no numeric limit.
deviations: The pass rule is the suite's own (decision D8): both the last and the mean exit time of the 24 zone-1 occupants are later in Scenario 1 than in Scenario 2. The disabled occupant is not part of either measure.

The scenario is built in code (standards/utils/movement_disability.py) rather than loaded from a scenario file. The builder sets the disabled occupant's desired speed at every step from its position, because the scenario harness applies speed zones to all agents.

The disabled occupant has a radius of 0.4 m (0.8 m wide) and a desired speed of 0.8 m/s on the flat and 0.4 m/s on the ramp. The other 24 occupants walk at 1.25 m/s everywhere, including on the ramp, with the suite's default radius of 0.15 m.
The ramp is flat. The 1 m height difference between the rooms is not modelled. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Exit route allocation
tests.definition: Twelve rooms line a corridor section, six on each side, with a main exit and a secondary exit. Occupants have speeds and characteristics from the expected building population and no pre-evacuation time. The occupants of rooms 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 are allocated to the main exit and all others to the secondary exit. The tester reports how the destination is set and whether the allocation is a user-defined deterministic one or comes from a predictive sub-model.
tests.expected: Every occupant moves to the exit it was allocated to. ISO calls the test a qualitative verification of the model's assignment.
deviations: ISO's text and its figure disagree. Table 9 gives 23 agents. Figure 5 marks one person in each room except room 3, which has two, which is 13 agents. The suite follows the text: 23 agents, two in each room except one in room 3.

The allocation is a user-defined, deterministic journey per room. The pass rule is the suite's own: after the run every agent's nearest exit, measured from its final position, is the exit allocated to its starting room.
All agents walk at a constant 1.3 m/s instead of a speed distribution from the building population.
The layout is redrawn from Figure 5 only approximately: the main exit is 0.9 m wide, and room outlines and exit positions differ in detail. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Dynamic availability of exit
tests.definition: A room of 10 m by 15 m has two 1 m wide exits, one on each 15 m wall, at equal distance from the short end wall. One occupant with no pre-evacuation time and a constant speed of 1 m/s is placed as in Figure 6. Exit 1 becomes unavailable after 1 s of simulated time, and the exit used by the occupant is recorded. The tester reports how the destination is set. A model that cannot change exit availability during a run documents that limitation.
tests.expected: The occupant does not use Exit 1.
deviations: Not run. The scenario harness (jupedsim-scenarios 0.7.3, the locked version) removes exits only before a run and has no runtime exit closure. The test forces a reroute by writing the runner's private agent state, so it would not exercise any public closure feature; it is marked not to run.
In the scenario file the occupant's initial exit is set by two journeys with equal weights, so the premise that it first heads for Exit 1 is not fixed by the scenario.

tests.title: Congestion in front of a flight of stairs
tests.definition: A room 8 m wide and 5 m deep opens through a 2 m wide corridor, 12 m long, to a flight of stairs going up (dimensions from Figure 7). One hundred and fifty occupants with no pre-evacuation time and speeds distributed as in the building population start in the room and walk to the stairs. The tester documents the population data.
tests.expected: Congestion forms at the exit of the room, a steady flow follows in the corridor, and congestion forms at the base of the stairs because corridor and stair have different flow characteristics. ISO calls the evaluation qualitative.
deviations: The stair is a flat zone with a speed factor of 0.5 that the test adds at y = 14 m to 20 m. The corridor is 15 m long in total, so the flat part is 9 m instead of 12 m. Congestion at the stair base is therefore driven by the input speed factor.

The pass rule is the suite's own: the peak density over the run in a 2 square metre window at the room exit and in one at the stair base must each exceed the peak density in a window in the middle of the corridor.
Desired speeds follow a Gaussian with mean 1.2 m/s and standard deviation 0.2 m/s, the suite's choice. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Maximum flow rates at an opening/exit
tests.definition: A room of 8 m by 5 m has a 1 m exit centred on the 5 m wall. One hundred occupants are placed in the room and assigned to the exit. The flow through the exit over the whole period is compared with a predefined maximum. ISO notes that the test is a verification if the model restricts door flow, and an external validation requirement if flow is emergent. The tester documents which of the two applies and, for emergent flow, defines the threshold from the model's own assumptions. Grid models show the sensitivity to discretisation.
tests.expected: The flow at the exit does not exceed the predefined maximum. ISO gives 1.33 persons per metre per second (MSC/Circ.1238) as an example value.
deviations: Decision D12: the test switches on the scenario harness's exit throughput limiter at 1.33 persons per second and checks that the measured flow stays at or below the limit (restricted-flow reading). The limiter belongs to the scenario harness, not to the simulation model. The flow without the limiter is printed and not asserted.

The pass rule is the suite's own: (N - 1) / (t_last - t_first) over the agents' last recorded frames, divided by the 1 m exit width, is at most 1.33 persons per metre per second plus a 1 % tolerance for trajectory sampling.
Occupants walk at a constant 1.2 m/s. No grid sensitivity applies. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Stair flow rates
tests.definition: Two floors 3 m apart are joined by a stair at 45 degrees with a diagonal of 4.24 m. Five stair widths are tested: 1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6 and 1.8 m. Two scenarios are run for each width: stair down and stair up. In each, 100 occupants with no pre-evacuation time and a speed of 1 m/s start uniformly distributed on one side of the stair. The average flow on the stair is determined for every combination. The tester reports whether the flow is emergent or user-defined.
tests.expected: A wider stair gives a higher flow rate. ISO sets no numeric limit.
deviations: Only one scenario is run. The stair is a flat zone, so up and down are identical by construction.
The stair is a flat 6 m strip with a speed factor of 0.5, so agents walk it at 0.5 m/s instead of 1 m/s. The feeding room is 10 m by 8 m.

The pass rule is the suite's own: the flow across the middle of the stair, (n - 1) / (t_last - t_first), has a positive linear trend over the five widths, the widest stair has a higher flow than the narrowest, and every width yields a flow value. It does not require an increase at every width step.
The scenario is built in code (standards/iso/scenario_builders/iso12_stair_flow.py) rather than loaded from a scenario file. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Relationship between flow rate, density and walking speeds in a corridor
tests.definition: A corridor of 60 m by 2 m is split into three zones of 20 m, with line A between zones 1 and 2 and line B between zones 2 and 3. Occupants with no pre-evacuation time and a speed of 1 m/s are spread uniformly over the whole corridor and walk to the exit on the right. The runs use 60, 120, 240, 360 and 480 occupants (initial densities 0.5, 1, 2, 3 and 4 persons per square metre). The last occupant in zone 2 is placed near line A, and the time it needs from A to B gives its walking speed. The flow at line B is averaged from the start until that occupant reaches B. The density in zone 2 is recorded when that occupant reaches the centre of the zone. The tester may vary the averaging intervals.
tests.expected: The speed against density and the flow against density in zone 2 are plotted and compared with the assumptions built into the model. ISO calls the test qualitative and sets no pass limit.
deviations: The test runs 60, 120 and 240 occupants only. The 360 and 480 cases are not run.

The pass rule is the suite's own: the mean zone-2 speed over line A to line B must not exceed the assigned 1.0 m/s by more than 0.05 m/s. Only agents that start upstream of line A and cross both lines are timed. Agents that start inside zone 2 are left out, because timing them from their first frame would overstate their speed.

ISO's protocol for the last occupant in zone 2 is not implemented: the speed is the mean over all agents that cross both lines. Density and flow at line B are computed by the scenario builder and not asserted.

Agents spawn inside a strip inset 0.3 m from the walls, so the initial density is about 1.4 times the nominal value. The scenario is built in code (standards/iso/scenario_builders/iso13_corridor_fd.py) rather than loaded from a scenario file. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Group behaviour
tests.definition: A room of 15 m by 20 m has a 1 m exit. Group 1 is five adults at the top of the room with no response time. Four walk at 1.25 m/s and the fifth at 0.5 m/s. Group 2 is ten slower adults at 0.2 m/s, spread uniformly in the central part of the room. Group 1 must reach the exit. The test asks whether a group sub-model keeps the group together, as proximity only, when its members differ in speed. A model without group behaviour documents that limitation.
tests.expected: The members of Group 1 reach the exit together: their arrival times differ by no more than 10 s. ISO states that 10 s is an arbitrary value chosen to allow a quantitative comparison.
deviations: Group 1 is homogeneous: all five members walk at 1.25 m/s. ISO's slow fifth member (0.5 m/s), which is the case that tests group cohesion, is not included. A pass shows that agents of equal speed arrive together and does not show group cohesion.
Group 2 walks at 0.5 m/s instead of 0.2 m/s.
The exit is 3 m wide instead of 1 m.
The threshold of 10 s is ISO's. Exit time is each agent's last recorded frame (decision D3). Group 1 is the five agents that start highest in the room. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Social influence on exit choice
tests.definition: A room of 10 m by 15 m has two 1 m exits on the 15 m walls, centred 12 m from the short end wall. In Scenario 1 one occupant (occupant 1), with no preferred exit, no pre-evacuation time and a speed of 1 m/s, starts 1 m from the bottom wall at a position equidistant from both exits. The run is repeated until the exit usage changes by less than 1 % with an additional run. In Scenario 2 a second occupant starts 2 m from the bottom wall and is deterministically assigned to Exit 2. The runs are again repeated until usage is stable. Exit usage is recorded. A model whose exit choice is user-defined, so that occupants always take the closest exit, documents that limitation.
tests.expected: Occupant 1 uses Exit 2 more often in Scenario 2 than in Scenario 1.
deviations: Scenario 1 has two free occupants instead of one, each assigned by journey weights of 50 / 50 to the two exits. The exit of the free occupants is set by these input weights, not by a choice the model makes. Their start positions are drawn inside a small box and are not fixed.
Scenario 2 adds a third occupant, bound to Exit 2, starting about 2 m from the bottom wall. The occupants that start closest to the bottom wall (below 1.5 m) are counted as the free ones.
ISO's rule of repeating until the exit usage varies by less than 1 % is replaced by 40 fixed seeds.
The pass rule is the suite's own: the Exit-2 fraction of the free occupants in Scenario 2 must be higher than in Scenario 1.

tests.title: Affiliation to familiar exits
tests.definition: A room of 10 m by 15 m has two 1 m exits on the 15 m walls, at equal distance from the short end wall. In Scenario 1 one occupant who is unfamiliar with the exits (no pre-evacuation time, 1 m/s) starts 1 m from the short wall at a fixed position equidistant from both exits. In Scenario 2 one occupant affiliated with Exit 2 starts at a position that ISO's text places in the central area at the start of the corridor. Each scenario is repeated until the exit usage changes by less than 1 % with an additional run. The test needs an exit-choice sub-model that represents familiarity. The tester documents whether affiliation has its own sub-model and whether exit choice is deterministic or predictive.
tests.expected: The usage of Exit 2 in Scenario 2 is higher than in Scenario 1.
deviations: Affiliation is represented by journey weights. Scenario 1 uses weights of 50 / 50. The affiliated case uses 20 / 80 in favour of Exit 2. The result follows from these input weights and from the harness's proportional split of agents over journeys. No affiliation sub-model is involved, as in NIST Verif.3.3.
Each scenario has two occupants instead of one. Both scenarios use the same start region.

The pass rule is the suite's own: with 50 / 50 weights the two exits differ in use by no more than 10 % of all arrivals, and with 20 / 80 weights Exit 2 is used more than Exit 1, over 20 fixed seeds. ISO's repeat-until-stable rule is not used.

tests.title: Route choice based on geometric layout
tests.definition: A two-floor structure joins a start area and a target area by two flights of stairs plus a corridor on the ground floor, and by a longer corridor on the upper floor. One occupant starts in the start area and is assigned to the target. The tester reports whether the route was specified by the user or came from the model's default route-choice algorithm. Models that handle groups in aggregate may run more than one occupant.
tests.expected: The occupant takes the short path through the lower floor or the longer path on the upper floor, and the path matches the route-choice algorithm of the model. ISO calls the test a qualitative check of the adopted behaviour.
deviations: Both floors are flattened into one 2D polygon. The stairs are strips with a speed factor of 0.5, and the lower corridor is drawn as a separate strip offset below the upper ring.
Ten agents at 1.2 m/s are run instead of one. Route choice is left to the model's default shortest-path routing.

The pass rule is the suite's own: the shortcut must be shorter than the long way on the suite's rough plan-view length estimates (which leave out the vertical offset of the lower corridor), and more than half of the ten agents must take it. An agent counts as taking the shortcut if it enters a stair strip.
The scenario is built in code (standards/iso/scenario_builders/iso17_route_choice.py) rather than loaded from a scenario file. One seed (42) is run.

tests.title: Reduced visibility vs walking speed
tests.definition: A corridor 2 m wide and 100 m long has a 1 m exit at its end. One occupant has a smoke-free walking speed of 1.25 m/s. A constant extinction coefficient of 1.0 per metre fills the corridor from the start, and no light sources are present. The occupant walks to the exit. The tester must know which speed-versus-visibility correlation the model uses and calculates the expected travel time by hand beforehand. The test is repeated with other combinations of smoke-free speed and extinction coefficient; ISO suggests speeds of 1.0, 0.75, 0.5 and 0.25 m/s and extinction coefficients of 10, 7.5, 3.0 and 0.5 per metre. Irritant and toxic effects are outside the test. A model without a visibility-speed sub-model documents the limitation.
tests.expected: The simulated travel time equals the hand-calculated time from the model's own correlation, that is, it agrees with the model's speed reduction factor.
deviations: Not implemented: there is no test for it in this suite. JuPedSim has no built-in speed reduction by visibility.

tests.title: Occupant incapacitation by fire/smoke
tests.definition: A 10 m by 10 m room, 3 m high, has no fire source. In step 1 one occupant stands in the centre, held in place by a very large pre-evacuation time. Hazardous conditions, such as toxic gases, irritants, heat or radiation, are imposed according to the incapacitation sub-model in use, and the time at which the occupant's fractional effective dose (FED) reaches 1 is determined. In step 2 the same FED is computed at the same location by hand calculation or by an independent validated fire model using the same FED formulation. The test is repeated for each hazard the sub-model contains. Moving occupants may be added as an extension. A model without such a sub-model documents the limitation.
tests.expected: The time to FED = 1 in the evacuation model equals the time to FED = 1 at the measurement point in step 2, for every hazard in the sub-model.
deviations: Not implemented: there is no test for it in this suite. JuPedSim has no built-in FED model.

tests.title: Lift usage
tests.definition: Two rooms lie 3.5 m apart in height and are joined by a lift. A 1 m exit is in room 1. One occupant with a speed of 1 m/s and no pre-evacuation time starts in room 2, and the lift is the only way out. The lift starts in room 1, travels to room 2, collects the occupant and takes it back to room 1. The tester defines the lift kinematics, such as speed, acceleration and door times. A model without a lift sub-model documents the limitation. A model that supports several lifts needs an additional test with at least two lifts, each with a capacity below the number of occupants.
tests.expected: The occupant first enters the lift in room 2, is discharged in room 1, and then reaches the exit of room 1. ISO calls the test a qualitative check of the model's assignment.
deviations: Not implemented: there is no test for it in this suite. JuPedSim has no lift component.

tests.title: Escalator usage
tests.definition: Two floors 3 m apart are joined by an escalator 2 m wide with a diagonal of 4.24 m at 45 degrees. In Scenario 1 one occupant (no pre-evacuation time, initial speed 1 m/s) rides down from the upper to the lower floor. In Scenario 2 one occupant rides up. The tester sets a modified speed on the escalator that differs from 1 m/s. The tester reports whether occupants can walk on a moving escalator and whether the model handles walkers and riders and side preference.
tests.expected: The occupant's final speed on the escalator accounts for the speed of the escalator. ISO calls the test a quantitative check of the speeds in both directions.
deviations: Not implemented: there is no test for it in this suite. JuPedSim has no escalator component.
